clue.text: Of refinement universal between sect and meeting

indicators.note: the universal letter is set between the words for sect and meeting, so it sits in the gap where they join

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect
a rally is a mass meeting
U is the British film certificate meaning universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Something refined and for everyone sits between a religious sect and a public meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' sets the universal letter in the gap between sect and meeting. U is the British film rating for a film anyone may see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cultural concerns the arts and polish of a society, so 'culturally' means in matters of refinement.

clue.text: Caught by Valentine on the leg

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Alf Valentine was a celebrated West Indies spin bowler of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A cricket scorecard: the batsman caught by Valentine, fielding on the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a cricket dismissal, 'c Valentine', with 'on the leg' sounding like the leg side of the field; in fact it defines a body part. Alf Valentine bowled spin for the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: The calf is the fleshy back part of the lower limb below the knee, so it is found on the leg.

clue.text: Wash an American city beneath

parts.note: LA is the usual abbreviation for Los Angeles
under is a direct synonym of beneath

explanation.surface: An instruction to clean something below a city in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder clothes is to wash and iron them.

clue.text: Pure age of the grown-up in a cockney pursued

indicators.note: the age of the grown-up is placed inside the cockney word for pursued
a Cockney Londoner traditionally drops the H at the start of words, so the opening H goes

parts.note: pursued means hunted
a grown-up is an adult
an era is an age

explanation.surface: Someone pure in their adult years, chased by a Londoner from the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cockney' gives UNTED: Cockneys, from London's East End, famously drop their aitches. 'in' then places the grown-up's age after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadulterated means unmixed with anything else, hence wholly pure.

clue.text: Sailor did the puzzle and was freed

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
to have solved something is to have done the puzzle

explanation.surface: A seaman finishes a puzzle and is released, perhaps from a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: To be absolved is to be released from guilt or obligation, so it is a synonym of set free.

clue.text: Words presented in a lovely rich melody

definitions.note: plural here, since a song's lyric is its words taken together

indicators.note: the letters are presented inside the run of words lovely rich, across the space between them

explanation.surface: Song words performed to a beautiful, full tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyric of a song is the text that is sung, as opposed to the music.

clue.text: Some writing about love produced by prophet

parts.note: a, as in a single something, stands for some

indicators.note: the writing goes about the letter for love, wrapping round it

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A prophet produces a text on the subject of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O (love, nil in tennis) between the M and S of A MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: It seems unusual in China

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Something looks strange while in the country of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is porcelain; the 'in' of the surface is fodder, and 'It' just introduces the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen is the German town that gave its name to a famous fine porcelain.

clue.text: Sweet relative who is lavishly treating the young

definitions.text: who is lavishly treating the young

parts.note: sugar is a sweet substance
daddy, a father, is a relative

explanation.surface: A kind relation who spoils the children.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a doting grandparent; the answer is an older man who spends lavishly on a much younger partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy older man who showers gifts on a youthful companion is called by this name.

clue.text: Woman who gets something subtle after she's fifty

indicators.note: the subtle something comes after the fifty, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an aura is a subtle atmosphere or emanation

explanation.surface: A woman acquires a certain air once she reaches fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Cancelling means of copying thing of art with science

parts.note: SC is an abbreviation for science, as in BSc

parts.words: means of copying thing of art
parts.note: a rubbing, such as a brass rubbing, copies a design by rubbing over paper laid on it

explanation.surface: Copying artworks with scientific methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrubbing a plan is informal for calling it off.

clue.text: Member of a group machines cover in a mouthful

indicators.note: the machines and cover go inside the word for a mouthful

parts.note: a bite is a mouthful
looms are weaving machines
to bury is to cover over

explanation.surface: Machines are tucked into a single bite of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' slips the machines and cover inside the mouthful just after its first letter. The Bloomsbury Group was a circle of London writers and artists including Virginia Woolf.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bloomsburyite belonged to the Bloomsbury Group, the early-twentieth-century set of English writers and artists.

clue.text: Traitor makes an exact counterpart angrier

parts.note: a double is an exact likeness of someone
crosser means angrier

explanation.surface: A turncoat creates a lookalike who is even more annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who double-crosses betrays a person they pretended to help.

clue.text: Bewildered old boy joined without an animal

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so joined wraps round the animal

parts.note: fused means joined
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A confused former pupil joined up without a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking, giving FUSCATED; read as 'lacking', the animal would be taken away instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obfuscated is made obscure or confused, close to bewildered.

clue.text: Obstruct a woman from making soft fibre

parts.note: to bar is to obstruct
Thea is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Blocking a woman from producing a gentle textile.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine soft cloth woven of wool, often with silk, used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Catkins give thanks to last word

definitions.note: plural, as amenta is the plural of amentum

parts.note: amen is the word ending a prayer
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Saying thank you after the final word of a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amentum is the botanical term for a catkin, a dangling flower spike, and amenta its plural.

clue.text: Blackguard and artist without the episcopal dignity

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the blackguard wraps round the word the

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A scoundrel and a painter lacking the dignity of a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside rather than lacking, giving CATHED; the word 'the' is letters in the answer, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedra is a bishop's throne, the seat of his authority, as in ex cathedra pronouncements.

clue.text: Remove stopper from United Nations port

parts.note: Cork is a port city in Ireland

explanation.surface: Taking the cap off a bottle shipped from a UN harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncork a bottle is to pull out its cork, the stopper.

clue.text: Messenger that is behind ancient city in Hebrew measure

indicators.note: the city and that-is pair go inside the Hebrew measure

parts.note: a cor is an ancient Hebrew measure of capacity

indicators.note: the that-is abbreviation sits behind the ancient city, so it follows it

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A messenger following an old city within an old measure of volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts the that-is abbreviation after the city; 'in' then sets that pair between the measure's O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier carries messages or parcels.

clue.text: Talked nonsense to make the stab be bloody

parts.note: a jab is a quick stab or poke
red is the colour of blood

explanation.surface: Someone gabbling about a stabbing that will draw blood.
explanation.definitionFit: To jabber is to talk rapidly and unintelligibly.

clue.text: Jackets for refrigerator ships?

definitions.meaning: short double-breasted coats of thick cloth, as worn by sailors
vessels with chilled holds for carrying frozen cargo

explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is both a heavy sailor's jacket and slang for a refrigerated cargo vessel.

clue.text: Recrimination in shopping attack

parts.note: a counter is where shopping is served
a charge is an attack

explanation.surface: An accusation made during a shopping assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A recrimination is an accusation made in reply to another, the same as a charge levelled back.

clue.text: Student without the right to become an author

indicators.note: without here means lacking, so the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: a reader is one who reads and studies
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A student turns writer once they lose the correct way.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a nineteenth-century English novelist and dramatist.

clue.text: Letters satisfy rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to sate is to satisfy

explanation.surface: Correspondence that pleases people, getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, so etas are characters of the script.

clue.text: Two previous owners mislaid hard thin old penny

indicators.note: mislaid suggests things put in the wrong place, so these letters are put in another order

parts.note: D, from Latin denarius, was the abbreviation for a penny before British decimal coinage in 1971

explanation.surface: A coin that has been through two hands, lost in a hard, thin state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaid' shuffles HARD THIN into THIRDHAN, then D, the pre-1971 British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something third-hand has come to you after two earlier holders, the first and second hands.

clue.text: Composer of the wild tribe

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of tribe run into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician who belongs to a savage people.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Ibert was a twentieth-century French composer.

clue.text: Room for development

parts.note: read as space to grow, it is in fact the word before room in the photographer's chamber where film is developed

explanation.definitionFit: A darkroom is the unlit room where photographic film and prints are developed.
